panels.narrative: In the dream, the stars did not twinkle; they pulsed with the rhythmic, cold precision of a heartbeat. Joel lay on a bed of dry grass, but the ground beneath him felt less like earth and more like a suggestion of solidity.
When he reached out to touch a nearby terebinth tree, his fingers didn't meet bark. Instead, the texture lagged.
For a fraction of a second, the tree was a grey, unrendered pillar of geometric planes before the brown ridges of the trunk snapped into existence, shivering with a late-calculated detail.
